small_guidance:
- The scatter kernel uses one program per input voxel × OC tile with atomic_add into the output; this serializes writes heavily. Increase BLOCK_OC to 32 or 64 (OC=16 fits in a single tile of 16) and drop atomics by having exactly one program per input voxel covering all OC at once (BLOCK_OC=16, single oc tile), eliminating the second grid dim.
- Hoist x_val loads outside the kd/kh/kw loops — load all 3 IC values once per program into registers, then reuse across all 27 kernel taps. Also precompute oc-stride weight base to reduce address arithmetic in the inner static_range.
- The finalize kernel does val/64 + bias then scale*..+shift, but the divide-by-64 should only apply to the pool-window sum; since the scatter only writes valid taps, pooled values at the border are scaled wrong. Verify and, if correct, fuse the *(1/64) into scale at host side (scale' = scale/64, shift' unchanged after folding bias) to remove one multiply.
large_guidance:
- Replace scatter-add + atomics with a gather-based direct ConvTranspose3d kernel: one program per (N, OC_tile, output-spatial tile of the *pooled* grid, i.e. OD×OH×OW). Each program computes a 4×4×4 pool window of pre-pool conv-transpose outputs by gathering the contributing input taps (input positions (od+pad-kd)/stride etc.) and accumulating directly into the pooled sum — fusing conv-transpose + BN + both avg-pools into a single kernel with no intermediate tensor and no atomics.
- Output spatial after two pool=2 is OD=OH=OW=16 (since conv-transpose out is 64), giving N·OC·16³ = 64·16·4096 = 4.2M output elements — perfect for one-program-per-output-tile GEMM-style. Tile (BLOCK_OC=16, BLOCK_SPATIAL=64) and reduce over IC·KD·KH·KW·64(pool) inside the program, using tl.dot if you reshape the inner reduction as a matmul (W[IC*K³, OC] × X_gather[BLOCK_SPATIAL, IC*K³]).
- Fold BN scale/shift and the 1/64 pool normalization into the epilogue of this single kernel; pre-fold scale*=1/64 host-side. Use channels_last layout for the input to make the IC reduction contiguous and coalesce loads across the GEMM-K dimension.
